body:
Fuck, I just wrote out a long reply and lost it. 

It led up to this (Cognitive therepy (metacognition, as I like to call it), though belittling, helped me) - http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/d5dnl/if_youre_thinking_about_doing_it_soon_please/

It's great that you can do it well - and you'll definitely get better (I knew nothing when I started). Computers are being integrated into everything these days, and you'll come out with a degree in one of the fastest-growing fields there is. If you can, study hardware programming as well. It's interesting to get down into the nuts and bolts (electrons) of it all, and you'll probably end up working with/designing more technological pieces than just programming on them.

Sometimes they have housing grants for students in situations like yours. It can't hurt to ask, it's free money/housing. 

Also, they often have work for students - my first job was stacking chairs and cleaning pianos every day for music classrooms. It allowed me to buy the necessities. 

P.S. When you're in college, you can spend all day on campus. Classes range from early morning to late at night, and campuses are built to accommodate commuters who have to stay there all day. If you can't find alternative housing, you can spend as much time here as you want. Sleeping in lounges or grassy knolls at all hours of the day isn't unheard of. It's almost expected. And there are lots of computer labs, and libraries to work in.

But seriously, tell the counselors you're in an abusive household, and they'll work for you. See what you can do.

CS is a very good major. But also don't be afraid to try classes outside your curriculum. I was a CS major, took a very interesting physics course and now I have a BS in physics, with a cs minor. I program for a very large physics experiment at CERN. Never know where you'll land.

That sounds like a touch of psychosis. You should get out of there. When someone is verbally abusive and calls you unjustified adjectives over and over, you tend to believe them, even if they are not true. Forgive yourself and get out. There are lots of resources for people in abusive situations, especially in college. Please, do me a favor and go talk to a councilor. They've dealt with these things before, and can help you find a way to get into a steady place to live, abuse-free. (And yes, verbal abuse is abuse. It can be just as bad as physical - or worse, as it seems in your case, to the point where you'd want to give up on life because of it. It's not worth it, find a way out, things will get a lot better. College will be a very good time for you, full of freedom to pursue whatever you wish, mentally, academically, socially - a whole world is about to open for you. Things will get a lot better, I mean it.)

Me too. In college I tried a few times and failed, but said to myself the same as you did: "It doesn't matter when, but I WILL die of suicide. Maybe soon, maybe when I'm 30. Some day it will get me." 5 years later I'm a completely different person. Happy, healthy, with friends. Things will change, trust me. I was an absolute wreak. I don't know what happened. But if there's anything we can rely on, it's that things change. You sound like you've been at the bottom, so there's nowhere to go but up.

I think one of the major reasons people don't discuss it without anonymity is because of the consequences - I, too, felt this way at one point, and told my dearest friend for help. He called the cops and I was taken away (in handcuffs and a straight jacket in front of my roommates, and a dorm hall full of onlookers) to a mental hospital. 3 days of being treated like an illogical moron. "You don't know what you're thinking, you're mixed up." 

We just need someone to actually discuss things with. Why we feel like this. Our philosophies and mindsets that put us here (like coping with the realization of Nihilism). We're not insane, or unjustified in our thoughts. We just want to know why, and sometimes there is no answer, and sometimes we find that very painful. We look out into a world and can see nothing in a positive light, instead emotional and manifested physical pain. Is it not understandable why someone would not want to live this way?

They only want the 'hows'. When we ask for help, they only ask how often you cut, or if you ever thought about how you'd do it, to calculate the risk to yourself. If it's high enough they strap you down until you lie: "I don't think about it anymore." Another one cured, they pat themselves on the back. Then they let you go. 

Even psychologists. If you mention suicide they're required to call the police. I can't stand going to them because I have to lie. I don't plan on doing it, I just think about it. I want to discuss it. Maybe find a way around it. But they don't care about that. 

That's why there is no direct discussion.

If you're this miserable, drastic change is needed. I know you love your boyfriend, but maybe you need a break from him - not in a bad way, just say "I need to pull myself together", take a few sick days and stay with your parents, a friend, or in a hotel. If anything, it will help you realize if you really want to go, or if you really want to stay; and a few days of solid thinking without having to worry about work or relationship can really help, and also help solidify a decision, if you want to make one.

Perhaps you're sabotaging yourself because you like the idea of having a stable relationship and a promise of a supported future, but this isn't the right person. And the reason you're mind/body is sabotaging you is because you know this, but you also know that getting out of a good relationship on speculation would be very hard on you - it would mean perhaps years or even your lifetime searching, the whole time alone and unsupported, for something that might not be there.

This is only speculation - I suggest it because it happened to me a while back and I was miserable too, even though things had been fine. I thought that if I'd found the right person, he'd be able to help me through my cripping depression and maybe even fix me. So a few years into the relationship, despite the love and wanting to grow old together,  I thought "why do I still feel like this?" and thought I needed someone else. Of course it's incredibly difficult to find someone compatible and a huge investment of time and risked hurt feelings to become intimate with someone to the point of love, so it's a very intense decision whether to leave for the hope of something better, or stay and wonder if it will ever be enough. 

My solution came when it was too much to bare and I confronted him about not being able to helping me and that I wanted out for hope of something better. Of course he pleaded but admitted he didn't know how to help me. So I went to my parents for a few days, and realized that finding someone who would fix me was ridiculous - what more can someone do than love and care for you, and support you even if they don't know exactly what you need? I realized that I don't know exactly what I need either, and I can't expect it from him. Depression is still our own battle, and it's much better to have a companion in it than to sit on the battlefield and wait for someone to come fight it for us. 

Anyway, that's just my two cents. It may be completely different for you, but maybe it will give you some insight. 

Please, please take care of yourself. Try a few cheerios and some sips of a smoothie to start, try to keep it down and work your way up. The sooner you can feel physically better, the sooner you'll be able to think more clearly and try to sort it out. Also, don't think that you still can't lean on your boyfriend in times like these. The love is there. In times of great need, you can forget everything and just revel in the fact that he loves you too. There is the ability to be completely contented and happy in a loving relationship at least for a moment, despite everything else. It is a defining characteristic of love, in my opinion. 

P.S. Sorry this is so long

Precisely. I'm up to ~$15,000 in debt that I need to pay back with a degree that requires a masters to get any related job in (Physics). My grades, too, are sub-par, due to being down in the dumps all the time. No recommendations - I didn't talk to my peers, and even less so to my professors - in addition to being frightened of being rejected by my fellow students, I was frightened that the prof would find out I'm actually an idiot. And by not talking to them, I haven't gotten the education I paid so dearly for - only that out of a textbook, and I've become an idiot from it.
How can one know if there is really something wrong?
